parsed.explanation: No documented traveller-facing universal exposure: no trans-specific border, entry-screening, facility or custody rule appears in the dossier, and legal gender recognition is resident-only and not scored. Same-sex conduct has been legal since 1990, so the sexuality statute is not a live lever. The main exposures are structural: pervasive LGBT violence and discrimination that police often ignore, no broad anti-discrimination law (the bill stalled), a council ban on a trans rights event, elite anti-trans rhetoric, and a school ban on LGBT discussion. Mitigations are narrow and mostly resident-facing: the 2016 social-name resolution covers health services, and the 2022 mental-health law has a non-discrimination clause. No trans-specific killing rate or visitor service-denial survey exists, so the violence axis is undocumented rather than low. Extrapolating from the weak recourse and hostile climate places this in the elevated band, below comparable jurisdictions with working protections.
